question: 已被验证成功的游戏团队实际通过什么流程确定美术风格？最终是什么让他们拍板？
method: Web search of first-party interviews, GDC talks and developer discussions (single verification pass, 2026-08-31). Exact URLs for new cases pending backfill; earlier leads already registered in art-direction-exploration.json source_leads.

cases.process: 70+ gameplay ideas in 6 months -> playable tofu-block ink prototype -> tried rabbit character, internally rejected ('why would a rabbit shoot ink') -> requirement list written by hands-on lead, including 'a motivation for which shooting ink makes sense' -> squid resolved all requirements at once.
cases.key_insight: Style was chosen by what the gameplay already was, not by visual comparison. The requirement list came after failures, not before.

cases.game: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
cases.process: Gameplay prototype first -> art director placed real legacy assets (Wind Waker / Twilight Princess / Skyward Sword) into the same HD scene for direct comparison -> Wind Waker style stood out -> but found it 'tells too large a lie' (players cannot use real-world intuition to predict physics/chemistry) -> slogan '清爽而有韵味' (gaseous, crisp yet flavorful) -> final approval took under one minute pointing at the screen.
cases.key_insight: Comparison happened on real in-engine content, not moodboards; the decision itself was a single authority's instant judgment made after the context was fully prepared.

cases.process: 8 years of development, discarded three or four entirely different games -> realistic military style failed in playtesting (art fights gameplay: soldiers hiding = invisible enemies; identical uniforms = indistinguishable classes) -> readability hierarchy distilled from failure (team > class > weapon) -> new concepts evaluated against the requirement list.
cases.key_insight: The requirement list was distilled from failures, never pre-written. Playtesting real content killed the wrong style.

cases.process: Game jam prototype -> 3-person team cannot do 3D -> sole artist (Ari Gibson): 'everything must be simply produced; characters must be really easy to draw, hence the minimal-line graphic style' -> whiteboard conversations, drawing on each other's work.
cases.key_insight: Style openly declared as a consequence of production capacity. No test battery existed.

cases.process: Rostov treats contemporary oil painting as the method itself -> hired painters first, game artists second -> even prop icons ground to oil-painting standard -> explicitly exempted from throughput and market constraints.
cases.key_insight: The counter-example: conviction-driven style with no constraint negotiation. Requires a strong artistic authority.

cases.process: Trusted art lead free exploration ('3 days silent, then drops a finished image; design team packages it backwards') -> capacity reality (9 people, no animator -> static art carries the game, Live2D only on dimension-marked exceptions) -> character anchors are story prototypes from One Thousand and One Nights, not capacity parameters.
cases.key_insight: Style grows from a trusted individual's free exploration; constraints define the boundary of presentation, not the style itself.

cases.process: Style derived from the world's own recording media (woodcut + manuscript illumination) -> many creative decisions decided by 'what we want the player to feel walking into the scene' -> high-fidelity manuscript plan rejected because of how players actually read the scene.
cases.key_insight: Medium-as-worldview: the style question equals 'what material does this world record itself with'.

cases.process: Author conviction (faithful 1930s cel animation) -> ~120,000 hand-drawn frames, ~80% slower than standard production -> accepted the cost knowingly.
cases.key_insight: Constraint knowingly absorbed because the conviction was non-negotiable.

cases.process: Painter-first origin (artist Conrad Roset's watercolor world preceded the game design) -> gameplay intentionally minimal, art carries the experience.
cases.key_insight: Same strong-individual route as Sultan; art precedes and leads design.

cases.process: Sole artist Bourassa externalized rules so he could 'art direct himself' -> hard edges / heavy blacks / no eyes all derived from gameplay systems (no compromise, lighting mechanic, soul consumption).
cases.key_insight: The single-artist-with-rules route: closest precedent for a no-artist team using externalized rules.

cross_case_rules: No studied team selected a style via a style beauty contest or scored comparison menu; the four-image menu approach has no industry precedent and is rejected.

Style judgment always happened on real content: playable prototypes, real legacy assets in-engine, or finished world-fragment images dropped by a trusted artist - never on abstract swatches or averaged prompt wallpapers.
Requirement lists were distilled from failures, not pre-written; pre-frozen test batteries (fixed character rosters, pre-declared exam criteria) have no precedent among the studied successes.
Final decision bases converge to four types: gameplay logic, production reality, author conviction, theme expression. Every project held at least one; most held two.
The final decision was a fast, single-authority judgment made after the context was fully prepared; process exists to accumulate that context, not to compute the answer.

implication_for_faust.production_model: user + AI as the 'art teacher' (user = eye/judgment, AI = hand). AI lacks muscle memory, so externalized style rules remain necessary - but they must be distilled from real-content iteration, not pre-declared.
implication_for_faust.default_exploration_path: Pick one direction the user's eye reacts to -> produce one real content artifact at true spec (e.g. a real game card) -> confront it in real use context -> let failures distill the requirement list -> iterate.
implication_for_faust.demoted_tools: same-content test battery, six-character exam roster, and scored weight comparison are downgraded to optional stress-test instruments, applied only after 2-3 directions already attract the user, with test content distilled from real content rather than frozen in advance.
implication_for_faust.authority_note: Per methodology data integrity rules, final style decisions belong to the user.
